Welcome to Hanborough Manor CE School
Community
Governors
Welcome to the Governors' section
For this academic year we are piloting a joint governing board over Freeland Primary and Hanborough Manor Schools.
They governors have responsibility for management of the school including working with the leadership team to set the strategic direction, appointing new staff, oversight of the school budget and looking after the premises and buildings. The governors try to be as proactive as possible and make regular visits into school.
The Governors are parents of children at school, staff at school, people appointed by the local Church, and people appointed by the Directing Board.
Chris Jones - Chair of Governors
(link governor for finance, whistleblowing and sustainability)
My name is Chris Jones, I am the Chair of Governors leading the board across the two schools for this pilot. I'm in my fourth year as parent governor at Hanborough Manor School with two children at the school. I have spent my career working across the government, commercial and education sectors leading or supporting research, education and innovation programmes with a focus on science and engineering. I am currently Director of Data & Digital Products at the Connected Places Catapult, a not-for-profit and the UK’s innovation accelerator for transport, the built environment, cities and local growth.
San​dra Einig - Safeguarding Governor and Parent Governor
(link governor for attendance, behaviour, data protection, maths, website compliance, monitoring and filterning)
My name is Sandra Einig and I am a parent governor with two children currently at the school. I serve on the Standards Committee. I am a Senior Lecturer in Accounting and Finance and also act as Finance Director for a local charity.
Nicholas Wood - Vice Chair - Director Appointed Governor
(link governor for SEND and Pupil Premium)
My​ name is Nicholas Wood and I am a Director-appointed governor. I have lived in Hanborough since 2017 and in West Oxfordshire since 1997. I have worked as a secondary teacher, a local church minister, and as an academic in Oxford University. I now work part-time for ARCh, an Oxfordshire educational charity supporting literacy in primary schools. I am a member of the Standards Committee and will be working especially in Special Educational Needs and Pupil Premium.
Diane Axford - Director Appointed Governor
(link governor for English)
​My name is Diane Axford. I am a director appointed governor and serve on the finance committee. I am an assistant head of a local primary school and have a wealth of experience in primary education. I have two children in secondary school and enjoy reading and walking in my spare time and also volunteer in several local community groups.
Marc Bransby - Parent Governor
(link governor for health and safety and complaints​)
My name is Marc Bransby I am a Project Management professional with 13 years military experience specializing in logistics management, facilities management, health and safety and customer service as well as a background in teaching and instructing. I am a parent governor with two children at Hanborough Manor School. I am currently the lead governor for health & safety, premises development and complaints. I am also a Level 2 England Hockey coach and Umpire and coach at Oxford Hawks HC.
Alex Wa​tson - Parent Governor
(link governor for Early Years)
My name is Alex Watson and I am a Parent Governor with two children, one of whom is currently at the school. I am the link governor for EYFS. Professionally, I have spent the last 12 years of my career in Data, Intelligence and Technology for Financial Services. Elsewhere I sit on the charity committee for Hanborough Preschool and in my spare time I enjoy cooking, travelling and exploring our wonderful local countryside.
Sarah Nickelson - Executive Head Teacher
I have been a Head Teacher since 2014 and am currently an Executive Head for Hanborough Manor CE School and Heyford Park School (Primary Phase). I am passionate about giving all children opportunities to learn in a safe and engaging environment; and aim to get the best out of every child. I am honoured to lead an amazing team at Hanborough Manor alongside our supportive governors.
Ian Jackson - Head of School
I am the​ Head of School at Hanborough Manor Primary School, as well as the English Lead for the school and the Strategic English Lead for the wider academy primary schools. I am passionate about education and committed to fostering children’s interests and passions early in life, helping them grow into confident, curious, and lifelong learners. I am incredibly proud to work at Hanborough Manor, where I feel fortunate to be part of a dedicated and inspiring team, all working together to provide the best possible opportunities for our pupils.
Rosie Potter - Staff Governor
My name is ​Rosie Potter and I am the teaching staff governor for Hanborough Manor. I am in my eighth year of teaching at Hanborough and am currently the Year 4 class teacher. I am also subject lead for Science and RE, and one of the school's Mental Health First Aiders.
Please contact office.3147@hanborough-manor.oxon.sch.uk for any information or documents from governor meetings.
Contacting Hanborough Governors
If you would like to contact the Governors please email the school office.

Welcome to Hanborough Manor CE School
SEND
Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCo) is Mrs Baker-Roberts. If you would like to contact Mrs Baker-Roberts, please telephone the school office on 01993 881446.
Please find below information regarding our core offer.
At Hanborough Manor CE Primary School, we are proud to be a fully inclusive school where every child is valued and supported to achieve their full potential. We believe that high-quality, appropriately differentiated teaching is the foundation for meeting the needs of all pupils, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
A child is identified as having SEND if they experience significantly greater difficulty in learning than others of the same age, or if a disability affects their access to education. We follow the Assess, Plan, Do, Review cycle to ensure that support is purposeful, effective and responsive. Progress is reviewed termly by teachers, the SENDCo and senior leaders, and provision is adapted to meet individual needs.
We support pupils across the four broad areas of need:
Communication and Interaction
Cognition and Learning
Social, Emotional and Mental Health
Sensory and/or Physical Needs
If a child is experiencing difficulties, concerns are discussed with parents and, where appropriate, the child may be placed on the SEND register to access additional support. Our SENDCo, Mrs Shannon Baker-Roberts, oversees all SEND provision and works closely with staff, families and external professionals.
Our Provision Includes:
High-quality adaptive teaching in every classroom
Small group and individual interventions tailored to need
Specialist programmes for literacy, numeracy, language and social skills
Emotional wellbeing and pastoral support (e.g. ELSA, Zones of Regulation)
Personalised support plans and Learning Plans for SEND pupils
Access to assistive technology and adapted resources
A fully accessible site with ramps and disabled facilities
We work with a wide range of external professionals including Educational Psychologists, Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists, CAMHS, SENSS teams and Inclusion Consultants.
Parents are central to our SEND process. Families meet with teachers three times a year to review progress and set new outcomes. Pupils are encouraged to share their views and be active participants in their learning.
Children with SEND are fully included in all aspects of school life, including trips and extracurricular activities. Reasonable adjustments and risk assessments ensure safe and equal access for all.
Where a child’s needs are complex and long-term, the school may apply for an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) in partnership with parents and the Local Authority.
Our aim is simple: To create a happy, nurturing and ambitious learning environment where every child feels valued, supported and able to succeed.

Welcome to Hanborough Manor CE School
Wrap Around Care
Wrap Around Care
The sessions that we are offering are: -
Monday - Friday: 8.00 - 8.45am at £4 per session (we are unable to provide breakfast, children should bring / have eaten their own breakfast)
Monday - Thursday: 3.00 - 5.45pm at £14 per session (a snack will be provided)
Wraparound Club Bookings
All Wraparound Club bookings (Breakfast and After School Clubs) must be made through your Arbor account.
Use the Arbor App or online portal with your registered email and password.
Navigate to ‘Clubs’:
On the main dashboard, tap ‘Clubs’ (use the ☰ menu on the app if needed).
Choose Breakfast Club or After School Club.
Choose Sessions & Pay:
Select your desired sessions and follow the prompts to complete payment.
Bookings are only confirmed once payment is made.
You can view bookings via the ‘Clubs’ section anytime.
If you use Childcare Vouchers or Tax-Free Childcare to pay for Wraparound:
Please continue using the same method as before.
Email the school office with:
Proof of payment and a short description of how much has been sent over and to which child's account the funds should be transferred to.
Children must be dropped off promptly at the main reception where they will be greeted by a member of staff. Those arriving after 8am should come to reception and ring the doorbell.
On collection (whenever is suitable for yourselves) please use the doorbell inside the main entrance to alert staff. Please do NOT use the staff car park.
With regard to managing safeguarding, health and safety, behaviour, emergency procedures, etc, we will be following the current school policies: https://www.hanboroughmanor.co.uk/policies/
